sentences.text:
THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
 THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  CRL.P No. 9451 of 2017  ORDER

A private complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C., was filed by the respondent, alleging that, the subject property was conveyed in favour of the complainant by accused No.1 by executing the registered sale deed after receiving sale consideration.
Such being the case, the complainant received the suit summons in O.S.No.96/2015, filed by the daughters of the accused No.1 claming their legitimate share in the subject property.

2. In the said suit, the complainant is arraigned as defendant No.6, and when the complainant issued legal notice to accused Nos.1 to 5, they have not replied to the legal notice and when the complainant enquired with the defendants No.6 and 7, they stated that, for commission amount,
they have kept quite and acted as mediators.
3. It was further alleged that, to make wrongful gain, by suppressing the truth, the accused Nos.1 to 5 have setup the daughters to file a false suit and the accused Nos.6 and 7 colluding with accused Nos.1 to 5 with an intention to cheat and defraud the complainant have given false evidence on created document.
4 . T h e c o g n i z a n c e t a k e n o f t h e o f f e n c e u n d e r S e c t i o n s 32,33,34,167,177,191,201,219,405,409,420,464,471 of IPC, by the learned Magistrate
is impugned in this petition by accused No.8.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner- accused No.8 submits that, the petitioner-accused No.8 who has only affixed his signature and seal as a notary to the sale deed executed in favour of the complainant, and except the said allegation, there is no allegation that he connived with other accused in setting up the daughters of the accused No.1 to file a suit for partition.
6. He further submits that the allegation against accused No.8 was made during the course of his duty i.e. notary.

The cognizance can be taken against a notary for the offence as specified under Section 13 of the Notaries Act, 1952, only upon a complaint in writing made by an officer authorised by the Central Government or a State Government and not by any other person.

7. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the respondent submits that, the allegation made in the complaint and also the sworn statement, clearly discloses the commission of the offence alleged against the petitioner- accused No.8, and the veracity of the allegations can be considered Sri. 8. I have examined the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

9. The allegation against the petitioner-accused No.8 is that he had affixed the seal and signature on the sale deed executed by the accused No.1 in favour of the complainant, and thus, he has connived with other accused in setting up the daughters of the accused No.1 to filed a false suit for partition.
10. The allegation against the petitioner-accused No.8 is during the course of discharge of his duty as a notary.

Section 13 of the Notaries Act, 1952, specifies that, No court shall take cognizance of any offence committed by a notary in the exercise or purported exercise of his functions under this Act save upon complaint in writing made by an officer authorised by the Central Government or a State Government by general or special order in this behalf.

11. In the instant case, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate on the basis of the private complaint filed by the respondent No.2 is one without authority of law and consequently, the cognizance taken of the aforesaid offences also stands vitiated.
12.
In view of the preceding analysis, I am of the considered view that, the continuation of the criminal proceedings against the petitioner-accused No.8 will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The Criminal Petition is allowed ii) The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.786/017, on the file of the Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, at Sira, insofar it relates to petitioner-accused No.8 is hereby quashed.
